definitions: To finish work for the day.
To reduce the price of something.
To produce something quickly and often carelessly.
To defeat or eliminate someone or something from a competition.
examples: We knocked off early on Friday.
They knocked off ten dollars from the original price.
The gang knocked off their rival.
He knocked off a watch from the display.
She knocked off a quick report before the meeting.
The underdog team knocked off the reigning champions.
